record.paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Can one extend the time interval over which the post-collision dynamics of a fast soliton on a graph is accurately approximated by outgoing solitary waves? More specifically, beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity timescale obtained in the paper, are there longer timescales of validity, perhaps depending on the initial data or on the vertex interaction, for which the outgoing-wave approximation remains accurate?

evidence.quote: Another important problem concerns the possibility of extending the timescale of validity of approximation by the solitary outgoing waves. In a different model (scattering of two solitons on the line) in [54], some considerations are given about the possibility of longer timescales of outgoing soliton approximation depending on the initial data and external potential, but it is unclear whether similar considerations can be applied to the present case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a star graph $\mathcal{G}$ consisting of $N$ half-lines joined at a single vertex $v$:
$$ i\partial_t \psi_j(t,x) = -\partial_x^2 \psi_j(t,x) - |\psi_j(t,x)|^2 \psi_j(t,x), \qquad x>0,\ j=1,\dots,N, $$
where $\psi=(\psi_1,\dots,\psi_N)$ satisfies a self-adjoint vertex condition at $v$ (for instance, a Kirchhoff or $\delta$-type condition characterized by a coupling parameter $\alpha$). Let
$$ \phi_v(x) = \sqrt{2}\, v\, \mathrm{sech}(v x)\, e^{i v^2 t/2}\, e^{i v x} $$
denote the standard fast solitary wave of velocity $v\gg 1$ on a single half-line, and consider initial data of the form $\psi(0,\cdot)$ supported on one edge and equal to a fast soliton of velocity $v$ traveling toward the vertex.

It is known that, after the collision with the vertex, the solution is approximated, in $H^1$ on each edge, by a superposition of outgoing solitary waves with reflection/transmission coefficients given by the linear scattering problem at $v$, and that this approximation is valid up to a timescale of order $\log v / v$ (logarithmic in the velocity).

Question: Can the time interval of validity of the outgoing-solitary-wave approximation for the post-collision dynamics be extended beyond this logarithmic-in-velocity timescale? In particular, do there exist longer timescales of validity—possibly depending on the initial data (such as its profile, phase, or energy) or on the choice of vertex interaction—on which the post-collision solution remains accurately approximated, in a suitable norm, by a sum of outgoing solitary waves with the prescribed scattering amplitudes?
artifact.category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
artifact.status_search_result: The available literature on fast soliton scattering on star graphs establishes a logarithmic-in-velocity timescale for the outgoing-soliton approximation, but no published result has been found extending this timescale or proving a sharp upper bound. Subsequent work on NLS on graphs has focused on stationary states, scattering and ground states rather than improving the post-collision time of validity, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fast solitons on star graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The outgoing waves preserve a soliton character over a time which depends on the logarithm of the velocity of the ingoing solitary wave.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the logarithmic-in-velocity timescale for the outgoing solitary wave approximation, leaving open whether longer timescales hold.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Another important problem concerns the possibility of extending the timescale of validity of approximation by the solitary outgoing waves.
status_evidence.claim: Explicitly lists the extension of the timescale as an open problem.
